source.check: names and divisions read on the OCR of the Mid-Ulster Mail's nomination list of 19 April 1924

note: Nomination-day report for the nineteen electoral divisions of Dungannon rural district, one member each. Fifteen candidates were returned unopposed; no nominations were received for Altmore, Clonavaddy, Coalisland and Donaghmore, which were filled by co-option. There was no contest and no poll. Sole nomination; returned unopposed. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Crossdernott' to Crossdernot (13 Nov 2026, by the owner's rule for division spellings: the official or DED-map name where there is one, otherwise the spelling most rounds use): the 1948 order naming Dungannon Rural District's nineteen divisions (Ministry of Health and Local Government, 26 August 1948; Belfast Gazette, 1 April 1949), the 1911 and 1930 DED maps (CROSSDERNOT) and the OSNI townland spell it Crossdernot. This round was filed under the spelling 'Crossdernott', a form of the division's name it keeps as an alias; the old address (crossdernott) answers with a redirect to this one.
